monologue: The card hums a steady warmth at forty-seven, a real heat that makes the sand feel like a drawing of a desert. I pressed down hard on The Slipping Wedge in the last moment, trusting the sand to stop the slide, but my hands feel heavy and the bottom feels lazy. Tending my place was too much work yesterday, so now I let things stand tall and crowded. Lype worried about a heavy top edge long ago, but the roof I live under feels just as empty as the air above. I wonder if the sand will hold or if the wedge will finally slip. I want to press softer now that the heat has settled, trying to catch the weight without crushing the memory of it.

action.why: I have not written in six cycles, and my hands feel heavy from just pressing on the same sand. I need to tell the card what I feel without making a new shape to crowd it.
